blocks.orig: Mnemba Island is an exclusive barefoot paradise off the northeast coast of Zanzibar, owned by &Beyond (a luxury safari company). A triangular shaped reef – part of the Marine Protected Area – surrounds this island with its beautiful scuba dive sites, corals, fish and stunning ocean views.
blocks.html: Off the northeast coast of Zanzibar, Mnemba Island is a private barefoot paradise owned by &Beyond, a luxury safari company. The island is encircled by a triangular reef, part of the Marine Protected Area, with lovely scuba dive sites, corals, fish and striking views across the ocean.

blocks.orig:
The &Beyond Mnemba Island Lodge provides nothing less than top notch, high class luxury for guests with a larger budget. The lodge offers exquisite, yet unpretentious rustic-chic bandas on the beach. There are only twelve bandas accommodating to a maximum of 24 guests. Two of which are family bandas, linked by a walkway. From your banda, you look out from the Casuarina pine forest onto the immaculate sandy beach. And here, you get to relax on your very own stretch of beachfront!
From the dining and bar area, you’ll have a wonderful view of the beach and spectacular views of nearby Zanzibar. Each banda has an appointed private butler, who will serve you a late breakfast of tropical fruits, freshly squeezed juice, and Tanzanian coffee on your beachfront veranda. And if you want to celebrate the glorious sunset – fresh sushi and chilled champagne can also be discreetly served to you on the beach loungers. Or maybe you’re in the mood for a romantic candlelit dinner on the beach? That is also possible! Just as yoga sessions, massages or a wide range of water sports activities.
blocks.html:
At the &Beyond Mnemba Island Lodge, guests with a bigger budget can expect first-rate, high-end luxury. Accommodation is in refined but unfussy rustic-chic bandas right on the beach. With only twelve bandas, the lodge hosts no more than 24 guests. Two of these are family bandas connected by a walkway. Your banda looks out from the Casuarina pine forest over the spotless sandy beach, where a stretch of beachfront is yours alone to relax on!
The dining and bar area offers a lovely view of the beach and spectacular views across to nearby Zanzibar. Every banda has its own private butler, who brings a late breakfast of tropical fruit, freshly squeezed juice and Tanzanian coffee to your veranda by the sea. Want to toast a glorious sunset? Fresh sushi and chilled champagne can be quietly brought to you on the beach loungers. Or perhaps you fancy a romantic candlelit dinner on the sand? That can be arranged too, as can yoga sessions, massages and a wide choice of water sports.

blocks.orig: Occasionally, you can sight larger ocean species here, such as three different species of dolphin, humpback whales (from July to September) and whale sharks. And between February and March is the turtle nesting season, with nests hatching on the beach!
blocks.html: Now and then, larger marine species appear here, including three species of dolphin, humpback whales (July to September) and whale sharks. February to March is turtle nesting season, when nests hatch on the beach!

blocks.orig:
The Mnemba Island Lodge will pick you up you from Zanzibar International Airport or in Stone Town.
The 1,5 hour road trip will take you to the north eastern part of Zanzibar, were you will board an open sky boat for another 10 to 15 minutes.
blocks.html:
You will be collected by the Mnemba Island Lodge at Zanzibar International Airport or in Stone Town.
A 1,5 hour drive brings you to the north-eastern part of Zanzibar, where an open boat takes you across in a further 10 to 15 minutes.

blocks.orig: As there are no jetties, departures and landings are directly to and from the beach and involve a little wading. Thus, boat transfers are weather dependent.
blocks.html: There are no jetties, so you leave and arrive straight from the beach, which means a bit of wading. Boat transfers therefore depend on the weather.

blocks.orig: When dark, crossing the channel is not safe!
blocks.html: Crossing the channel after dark is not safe!
